architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created a stateful widget pattern with Surface3D as state and VolatilitySurface as widget, following existing ratatui patterns
architecture_decisions.rationale: The ratatui library already uses StatefulWidget pattern extensively (e.g., in tests/stateful_widget_ref.rs). This approach separates rendering logic from state management, making the example consistent with library conventions and easier for users to understand and extend.
alternatives_considered: Creating a monolithic widget that manages its own state

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Used 2D grid structure (Vec<Vec<f64>>) for volatility surface data with separate strike and expiration vectors
architecture_decisions.rationale: The volatility surface naturally maps to a 2D grid where X-axis represents strike prices (moneyness) and Y-axis represents expiration times. This structure allows efficient row/column traversal for grid line rendering and matches financial data conventions.
alternatives_considered: Using a flat array with index calculations
Using a struct per data point with coordinates

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Used Braille marker for Canvas widget instead of block characters, providing 8x resolution
architecture_decisions.rationale: Braille characters (Marker::Braille) provide 2x4 dot resolution per character cell vs 1x1 for block characters. This enables smoother curves and higher detail in the 3D visualization without requiring more terminal space.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added colorgrad dependency for perceptually uniform color gradients and created custom palette system
architecture_decisions.rationale: The colorgrad crate provides scientifically accurate color gradients (viridis, plasma, inferno) that are perceptually uniform and colorblind-friendly. Custom palettes (phosphor, fear, calm) were added for visual variety while maintaining readability.
alternatives_considered: Using ratatui's built-in color palette only

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented keyboard controls following vim-style (hjkl) and arrow key conventions with real-time response
architecture_decisions.rationale: Using both vim-style (hjkl) and arrow keys accommodates different user preferences. The controls provide immediate visual feedback with smooth rotation/zoom, enhancing the interactive demo experience.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented 50 FPS target with delta-time based updates and FPS counter for performance monitoring
architecture_decisions.rationale: 50 FPS provides smooth animation while being conservative on CPU usage. The FpsCounter helps users understand performance characteristics and ensures the example runs well across different terminal emulators.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented proper 3D perspective projection with rotation matrices and camera distance
architecture_decisions.rationale: True perspective projection (dividing by distance) creates realistic 3D appearance where distant objects appear smaller. Rotation matrices around X and Z axes allow natural exploration of the 3D surface from any angle.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created comprehensive README with usage instructions and VHS tape for animated demo
architecture_decisions.rationale: The README provides immediate context for users, while the VHS tape (volatility-surface.tape) generates an animated GIF demonstrating the interactive features. This follows existing ratatui example patterns and serves as both documentation and marketing material.

implementation_summary:
The implementation creates a sophisticated 3D volatility surface visualization example that demonstrates advanced terminal graphics capabilities in ratatui. The core architecture follows the library's established StatefulWidget pattern, separating the rendering logic (VolatilitySurface widget) from the interactive state (Surface3D struct). This makes the example immediately familiar to existing ratatui users and demonstrates best practices for widget development.

Key technical achievements include proper 3D perspective projection using rotation matrices and camera distance calculations, which creates realistic depth perception. The use of Braille markers for the Canvas widget provides 8x higher resolution than block characters, enabling smooth curves in the wireframe visualization. The color system leverages the colorgrad crate for perceptually uniform gradients while adding custom palettes for visual variety.

The example integrates seamlessly with existing ratatui patterns: it uses the same layout system, follows the example app structure with proper Cargo.toml workspace inheritance, and includes a VHS tape for automated demo generation like other examples. The synthetic data generation in VolatilityEngine creates realistic financial volatility surfaces with time-based animation, making the example self-contained without external dependencies. Interactive controls support both vim-style (hjkl) and arrow keys, with smooth 50 FPS animation and performance monitoring via an FPS counter.
